institution: Conservatorium van Amsterdam (CvA) — Amsterdam University of the Arts (AHK)
accreditationStatus: NVAO-accredited — part of the accredited Master of Music (Master Muziek) of Amsterdamse Hogeschool voor de Kunsten (AHK). AHK is a government-funded (bekostigd) HBO institution and therefore an IND recognised sponsor for study residence permits.
whatYouStudy: Spatial/3D audio: Dolby Atmos, binaural, ambisonics. Year 1 foundation modules in immersive production across classical, jazz, pop and electronic genres, plus acoustics, mixing, production and management. Year 2 specialisation in either composing OR production for immersive audio, with research and capstone project. Tools: Pro Tools, Ableton Live, SPAT Revolution, for both studio production and live performance.
entryRequirements: 'A bachelor's degree (BA) in Music or a closely related field is required.' 'Significant experience in audio engineering at a professional level is required.' 'Proficiency in using software such Pro Tools (or main DAW), Ableton, or other industry-standard digital audio workstations is required.'
acceptsNonMusic: PARTIAL — 'Candidates with degrees in sound engineering or music technology (e.g., Abbey Road Institute, SAE, or equivalent) may also be considered.' A BSc Software Engineering is NOT named; the closest the page allows is 'a closely related field'. The binding obstacle is not the degree but 'significant experience in audio engineering at a professional level', which this candidate does not have. Realistically out of reach without several years of studio work.
portfolioSpec: Motivation letter (max 500 words); CV; THREE high-quality stereo recordings demonstrating diverse styles; optional research proposal.
auditionSpec: YES — live/online assessment: a 10-minute interview PLUS a 10-minute on-the-spot Pro Tools mixing test of a 24-track session.
tuitionNonEU: €8,250 per year — AHK institutional tuition fee 2026-2027 for non-EEA students, most Bachelor's and Master's programmes (statutory EEA fee €2,694). 2025-2026 rate was €7,375. Fees rise annually, so expect roughly €8,700–9,200 for 2027-2028 — UNVERIFIED for 2027-28.
otherFees: UNVERIFIED — instrument/studio costs not published. Dutch student residence permit requires proof of living funds (approx €1,100–1,200/month) set annually by IND.
totalCostEstimate: Tuition approx €16,500 for two years at the 2026-27 rate, plus living costs in Amsterdam of roughly €14,000–17,000/yr. Two-year total approx €48,000–52,000.
scholarships: AHK participates in the NL-Scholarship (formerly Holland Scholarship): €5,000 one-off in the first year, for non-EEA students starting a first bachelor or master at a Dutch institution. See https://www.ahk.nl/en/nl-scholarship/ — exact AHK deadline and number of awards UNVERIFIED. No CvA programme-specific scholarship for Immersive Audio was found.
languageRequirement: English. Candidates from non-English-speaking countries outside EU/EEA must present a language certificate.
englishTest: IELTS Academic 6.0 (Master); or TOEFL iBT 72; or Cambridge English 169.
deadline: 1 March (2026 cycle: 1 March 2026). For September 2027 entry expect 1 March 2027 — UNVERIFIED until the 2027 calendar is published.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — CvA typically opens applications in the autumn preceding the deadline (around October).

institution: Conservatorium van Amsterdam (CvA) — Amsterdam University of the Arts (AHK)
accreditationStatus: NVAO-accredited — part of the accredited Master of Music of Amsterdamse Hogeschool voor de Kunsten (AHK). AHK is government-funded and an IND recognised sponsor.
whatYouStudy: Combining acoustic instruments with live electronics through performance, composition, improvisation and multimedia. Max/MSP and Ableton Live, sound spatialisation, synthesizer programming, electroacoustic techniques, interactive video, notation for electronic performance, professional practice.
entryRequirements: 'The Live Electronics programme is intended for performers with an instrumental bachelor's degree or equivalent. Candidates with a bachelor's degree in another musical field may be admitted, provided that they show proficiency in music theory and a sufficient level of performance skills.'
acceptsNonMusic: NO (effectively). The quoted text extends admission only to 'a bachelor's degree in another musical field' — i.e. still a music degree — and demands proven music theory and performance skills. A BSc Software Engineering with no conservatoire training does not meet this. Rule out.
portfolioSpec: 'students are requested to send links to (an) audio and/or video recording(s) of a performance of live electronic music. A motivation letter stating the student's reasons for applying to the programme must also be included.' No fixed number of works or maximum duration stated.
auditionSpec: YES — live audition: 'a live electronic performance of no more than 10 minutes, followed by an interview of about 10 minutes.'
tuitionNonEU: €8,250 per year — AHK institutional fee 2026-2027 for non-EEA students (statutory EEA fee €2,694).
otherFees: UNVERIFIED. IND living-funds proof required for the residence permit.
totalCostEstimate: Approx €16,500 tuition over two years plus roughly €14,000–17,000/yr living costs in Amsterdam; two-year total approx €48,000–52,000.
scholarships: NL-Scholarship €5,000 one-off, first year, non-EEA students. https://www.ahk.nl/en/nl-scholarship/ — AHK-specific deadline UNVERIFIED.
languageRequirement: English; language certificate required for non-EU/EEA candidates from non-English-speaking countries.
englishTest: IELTS Academic 6.0 (Master); TOEFL iBT 72; Cambridge English 169.
deadline: 1 March (2026 cycle: 1 March 2026). Expect 1 March 2027 for September 2027 entry — UNVERIFIED.
